pack.name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0 architecture baseline
pack.description: Architecture checks mapped to selected OWASP ASVS 5.0 requirements. Not an OWASP certification or application test.

rules.title: Authentication boundary
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify the authentication authority, trust boundary, and protection applied before an application accepts a session.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document the identity provider, token validation boundary, session lifetime, and failure behavior.

rules.title: Credential and secret handling
rules.description: Architecture evidence should show where application credentials are stored, how access is granted, and how rotation is performed.
rules.remediationGuidance: Use managed identity or a governed secret store and record rotation ownership.

rules.title: Authorization enforcement
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify the component that enforces resource and function authorization for every trust boundary.
rules.remediationGuidance: Map roles, resource ownership, tenant scope, and denial behavior to the authorization boundary.

rules.title: Input validation boundary
rules.description: Architecture evidence should show where untrusted input is validated before it reaches interpreters, data stores, or downstream services.
rules.remediationGuidance: Identify validation ownership and reject or constrain unexpected input at each service boundary.

rules.title: Output and browser boundary
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify the controls that prevent untrusted output from becoming active content in a client or browser.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document encoding, content policy, and browser boundary ownership for user-controlled output.

rules.title: Cryptographic services
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify approved cryptographic services, key ownership, and the data flows that require protection.
rules.remediationGuidance: Map encryption in transit and at rest to keys, rotation, recovery, and service boundaries.

rules.title: Error and exception handling
rules.description: Architecture evidence should show how failures are contained, logged, and returned without exposing sensitive implementation details.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document error ownership, safe client responses, correlation identifiers, and protected diagnostic storage.

rules.title: Data protection and privacy
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify sensitive data classes, their storage locations, retention, and access boundaries.
rules.remediationGuidance: Connect data classification to storage, access, deletion, export, and monitoring controls.

rules.title: Communication security
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify protected communication paths between clients, services, data stores, and external dependencies.
rules.remediationGuidance: Use authenticated encrypted channels and document termination, validation, and private connectivity points.

rules.title: Malicious code and dependency controls
rules.description: Architecture evidence should show how third-party components and build outputs are selected, scanned, and promoted.
rules.remediationGuidance: Record dependency provenance, scanning, approval, artifact integrity, and rollback ownership.

rules.title: Business logic abuse boundaries
rules.description: Architecture evidence should identify rate, quota, replay, and workflow controls for operations that can be abused at scale.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document abuse assumptions, throttling ownership, idempotency, and escalation signals.

rules.title: Secure development architecture
rules.description: Architecture evidence should connect security requirements, design review, testing, deployment approval, and residual risk ownership.
rules.remediationGuidance: Maintain a trace from security requirements to architecture decisions, test evidence, and approved residual risks.
